title: ShortBurst reserve charging model and operator playbook
creator: Rina Patel
description: Context: Customers using Dedicated capacity request short-lived additional throughput above their reserved fleet. Existing surge pools cover many cases, but we see two common pain points: (1) short spikes (minutes) where allocation and billing granularity cause awkward per-minute overages and dispute volume, and (2) operator friction when manually approving or reclaiming ephemeral capacity. Goal: design and implement a ShortBurst reserve — a lightweight, low-latency ephemeral capacity lease mechanism with a clear charging model, deterministic decay behavior, and an operator playbook for exceptional handling. This ticket covers the charging model, required product signals for the autoscaler and console, operator runbook, and acceptance criteria for safe rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Define a billing model that charges a short, discounted per-minute rate for ShortBurst leases and includes a predictable decay window (default 10 minutes) to avoid surprise invoices.
A2: Implement ShortBurst API and autoscaler hook that can provision <= 8 GPU slots in <30s for eligible dedicated fleets and releases them automatically after the lease or when idle.
A3: Console UI surfaces ShortBurst usage (per-lease), projected invoice impact, and a one-click operator reclaim action that safely drains KV caches and migrates in-flight requests.
A4: Telemetry: emit shortburst.lease.start, .lease.end, .reclaim.initiated, .billing.charge_estimate with lease_id and effective_duration tags.
A5: Operator playbook documented in runbook and dry-run executed by SRE on staging with a simulated tenant; no customer-facing regression for 7 days post-rollout.
A6: Legal/billing sign-off on invoice sample language and dispute workflow.
A7: Metrics show median lease provisioning latency < 40s and tail (p95) < 90s in staging under 2x background load.
A8: Where ShortBurst overlaps existing surge-pool features, define deterministic precedence and automatic fallback to surge-pool when ShortBurst capacity exhausted.
A9: Backwards-compatible: customers without ShortBurst enabled see no change in existing surge billing or capacity behavior.
A10: E2E tests for lease creation, early reclaim, expiration billing, and console visibility included in CI.
design_notes: High level: ShortBurst is a temporal lease bounded by (fleet_id, lease_id). Leases are requested via a new endpoint POST /v1/dedicated/fleets/:id/shortburst with parameters: requested_slots (1-8), max_seconds (min 60, max 3600), and optional reason_tag.

Charging model proposal: base_reserved_rate * burst_multiplier * duration_minutes with a capped minimum billable block of 1 minute and a linear decay credit applied if operator reclaims within the grace window. Default burst_multiplier=0.5 (discounted vs on-demand because capacity is provisional and short-lived). Example: fleet reserved rate $5/hr/GPU -> per-minute reserved rate = $0.0833 -> ShortBurst per-minute = $0.0417; 7-minute lease yields $0.2919 billed. If reclaimed at minute 3 under a 10-minute decay window, apply a decay credit equal to 50% of remaining unused minutes to reduce billed amount, and surface the credit on next invoice line as 'ShortBurst decay credit'.

Decay window rationale: smoothing invoice spikes for very short leases reduces disputes and encourages polite usage for microbursts; default 10 minutes balances revenue predictability and customer experience. The decay window should be configurable per-tenant contract for enterprise customers.

Autoscaler integration: autoscaler receives a lease_token and priority tag. ShortBurst allocations are treated as preemptible relative to dedicated pinned workloads and must be reclaimable via the same preemption protocol used by surge pools (SIG_RECLAIM). On reclaim, autoscaler performs KV cache checkpoint and returns lease state to the controller within 30s.

Operator reclaim flow: console shows lease detail -> operator clicks 'Reclaim' -> controller marks lease for graceful drain, sets max_accepting_new_connections=false, sends reclaim signal to serving nodes, waits up to 45s for in-flight tokens to complete, then force-evicts. For safe reclaim ensure we snapshot ephemeral KV to ephemeral storage to allow quick resumption if lease is reissued to same hardware within 5 minutes.

Precedence and fallback: If multiple burst mechanisms requested concurrently, ShortBurst takes precedence for requests using lease_token; if ShortBurst capacity exhausted within a region, automatically attempt surge-pool fallback and bill using surge-pool semantics (separate invoice line).

Edge cases: aborted leases (created but no requests served) are auto-canceled after 120s and not billed. Leases exceeding max_seconds are terminated; partial-minute rounding rules apply consistently across all lease terminations.

DB changes: new table shortburst_leases (lease_id, fleet_id, requested_slots, allocated_nodes, start_ts, end_ts, status, billed_minutes, reclaim_reason). Schema owned by capacity service. (Note: implement as top-level flat table; DB migration ticket to follow).
Security & billing considerations: KMS keys used for any ephemeral KV snapshots; billing estimator should not leak customer pricing tiers in console when viewed by non-billing roles.
Observability: add dashboards for lease volume, avg duration, reclaimed fraction, avg reclaim latency, billing delta vs on-demand, and disputes count.
Open questions: should we allow cross-fleet aggregation leases (single lease spanning multiple small fleets)? Proposal: not in v1. Evaluate v2 after adoption data.
Alternate charging considered: flat per-lease fee (e.g., $0.10/lease) + small per-minute charge. Rejected for v1 because it complicates prorating and discounts for large enterprises.
Release plan: gated feature flag per-account; pilot with 8 select customers for 4 weeks then open to self-serve on-console for all Dedicated accounts.
Console UX: new 'ShortBurst history' column under Fleet Usage with per-lease expand/collapse and invoice preview modal that shows estimated vs actual charge.

API contract: shortburst.lease.create -> returns lease_id, allocated_slots, expires_at, invoice_estimate_id; shortburst.lease.query -> status + billing_estimate; shortburst.lease.cancel -> initiates reclaim and returns reclaim_eta.
Billing pipeline: create invoice_line_type = SHORTBURST_LEASE with meta tags lease_id, lease_duration_minutes, decay_credit_applied.
Operator docs: include a staged checklist for reclaim (check running jobs, notify customer via optional channel, run reclaim, escalate to SRE if eviction fails > 2 minutes).
